title: Head 6 · Indexing & memory
subtitle: Stages embed_images, embed_texts, link, latest and finish: making each frame searchable, proving the data is whole, and remembering where each object was last seen.
meta: Built and in use on the Pixel 9 Pro XL. "Crop any object" for last seen is proven on the laptop only.
Frame vectors, caption keywords and vectors, the link check, latest sighting per object and its 0.87 cut-off, any-object crops and DINOv2 (tried), finish.
EYKO-11 (image vectors), EYKO-12 (text vectors + keywords), EYKO-14 (link), EYKO-15 (latest sighting), EYKO-16 (finish), EYKO-62 (any-object crops, laptop), EYKO-64 (phone timing, open).
Head 6 · Indexing & memory: storing what each frame holds

sections.title: Summary
blocks: Once a frame is described, five stages make it part of the memory:

bullets: **embed_images** stores the frame's 512-d MobileCLIP vector (already made in dedup) so it can be searched by picture;
**embed_texts** stores the caption with a keyword index and a 384-d bge-small vector;
**link** runs ten SQL counts that must all be zero, proving every kept frame has everything it needs;
**latest** crops each detected object, matches it with earlier sightings and marks the newest one as latest;
**finish** deletes dropped pictures, marks the video ready and tells the person.

sections.title: Approach
blocks: Each kept frame's 512-d MobileCLIP vector, saved by the dedup stage, is written to image_vec as a float32 BLOB. No second model run: under 1 ms per frame.

bullets: Every caption (and every transcript chunk once speech lands) goes into video_texts with a keyword index.
bge-small-en-v1.5 runs on the phone from the repository's own ONNX file (133 MB) with a WordPiece tokenizer written in Kotlin. 26 ms per caption; cosine 1.0 against the laptop.
The 384-d vector is written to text_vec.
The phone's SQLite has FTS4, not FTS5, so the keyword index cannot rank with BM25 yet.

blocks.h3: link (EYKO-14): a check, not a repair

blocks: Ten SQL counts must be zero: every kept frame has its hash, scene record and vector; every time is inside the video; no row points at a missing video. If any count is not zero, the job fails with the reason. The stage never fixes data, so bugs show up instead of being hidden.

steps: Every object box of at least 16 px in a scene record is cropped (a square around the box) and turned into a MobileCLIP vector.
It is compared with earlier sightings of the same name in other frames and videos.
Same name and crop cosine ≥ **0.87** means the same object.
The newest sighting of each object is marked latest in object_sightings.

blocks: Deletes the JPEG files of dropped frames, marks the video ready, shows a notice. Retry restarts a failed stage.

sections.title: Tests and evidence

blocks.h3: The 0.87 cut-off (13 Oct, Pixel, six clips)

blocks: 90 object crops; the AI assistant grouped 54 of them into 24 physical things. 48 same-object pairs and 288 different-object pairs with the same detector name.
The two groups overlap between 0.77 and 0.92. About 540–567 ms per crop on the Pixel.
Baseline (EYKO-55): success 33.3 %, but the object was ever cropped by our detectors only 12.8 % of the time; most hits came from the closest crop, not the 0.87 rule.

blocks.h3: Storage cost (Ego4D on the Pixel, 27.8 min)

blocks: Captions 19 KB (0.7 KB per minute; VLM captions 3.6–5 KB). Database grew about 7 MB with every vector. Frame JPEGs were 8.8 MB per minute before EYKO-59.

bullets: Every kept frame is searchable by picture (image_vec) and by caption (keywords + text_vec).
A finished video is proven whole by the link check.
Each detected object has a latest sighting across videos, the basis for "where did I last see my keys?".
The same-object pairs were the easy kind and their grouping was AI-made, not checked by a person; real use will be worse.
The app only remembers objects its detectors name; Ego4D asks about any object.
Any-object crops and DINOv2 were measured on the laptop with a script that re-decodes frames by seeking; compare changes only within one script.
FTS4 keyword index: no BM25 ranking yet.
